kioshi keishicho.name: Kioshi Keishicho
kioshi keishicho.species: Human mutate. Dead man resurrected through magic and bonded to a suit of armor.
kioshi keishicho.origin: ===Origin=== Kioshi Keishicho was a police officer in Japan. He was killed by the Silver Samurai during his time as a villain. In the Japanese underworld of Yomi, Kioshi was approached by Amatsu-Mikaboshi, who offered to resurrect Kioshi so he could seek vengeance on the Samurai. Kioshi agreed, and returned to Earth, bonded to a suit of armor that was the dark mirror of the Silver Samurai's armor. He became the Ebon Samurai. Kioshi sought out Silver Samurai at the headquarters of the Big Hero 6, but found that his prey had already departed the team. The Ebon Samurai joined Big Hero 6 in Silver Samurai's place, biding his time until his chosen enemy resurfaced. ===Big Hero 6=== As member of Big Hero 6, Ebon Samurai and the rest of the team fell victim to a mind-control device secretly implanted within Baymax, prompting Big Hero 6 to travel to Canada and attack Alpha Flight. ===Civil War=== After the super-human Civil War, instead of forcing heroes to join the Japan Defense Agency, the Japanese government preferred to establish a voluntary public partnership with the Japanese super-heroes, including the Big Hero Six. To reaffirm this stand, senior officials from the Japanese Department of Supernatural Sciences (JDSS) held a press conference at the National Diet Building in Tokyo's Chiyoda Ward, with the Big Hero Six (Honey Lemon, Go-Go Tomago, Baymax, Hiro Takachiho, Sunpyre, and Ebon Samurai), along with the super-soldier Otomo and Red Ronin. ===Microverse=== thumb|left|Ebon Samurai While the other members of Big Hero 6 were on assignment in the United States, Ebon Samurai remained in Japan with Sunpyre and defended Big Hero 6 headquarters from an attack by the super-villain Deadline. Afterward, Ebon Samurai and Sunpyre decided to leave Big Hero 6 behind and travel to the Microverse planet of Ravellon to assist Sunpyre's mother, the exiled Empress Hynodia, in retaking her homeworld of Coronar from the fanatical Scions of the Azure Flame.

kioto.name: Kioto
kioto.origin: Captain Kioto was a member of the Imperial Japanese army during World War II. He and his troops occupied the island Tibula in the South Pacific Ocean, having convinced the natives that lived there to allow them to occupy their land. Kioto took perverse pleasure by torturing American prisoners of war until they died. He then had their bodies parachuted at a nearby military base. Due to the number of islands around the vicinity, American military officials estimated that it would take them months to learn the location where their soldiers were being tortured and killed. That all changed in the fall of 1943, when the leader of the natives protested to Kioto about not being allowed to have guns when they were charged with guarding the American prisoners. Kioto shot and killed the leader for this demand, hoping it would keep the natives from revolting. This had the opposite effect, as one of the natives traveled to the American base and left a map showing where the Japanese were camped. This map was found by Private Steve Rogers, who went to investigate with in his costumed identity of Captain America along with his partner Bucky. Helping the natives in a revolt to overthrow the Japanese invading their land, Captain America and Bucky were captured and brought before Kioto. Kioto told the heroes that he would execute them and send their bodies back to the American base as a warning to them. However, the two heroes managed to escape, and after raiding an ammunition hut and freeing the remaining American soldiers, led a counter attack on Kioto and his men. During the battle, they radioed the American base and gave the location of the island. Cap and the others managed to escape the island just as American bombers arrived. If Kioto was not killed during the fighting, he was surely eliminated in the subsequent bombing by American planes.

kip holm.name: Kip Hölm
kip holm.origin: Kip Hölm was a member of the Scania, a seafaring humanoid race who had settled on the planet Windhölme as refugees almost 300 years before Kip was born. Kip's parents were Gunnar Hölm, a respected Fleet Captain of the Western Isles and a member of the planet's High Council, and his wife, Marie. As kip grew up, he developed certain certain high-range psychic talents, making him what the Scania called a Windrunner. When Kip was seventeen years old, Windhölme was attacked by well-trained mercenaries intent on wiping out most of the population and taking the survivors as slaves. Among the earliest victims were Kip's parents who were incinerated before his eyes by a direct hit from an energy bolt fired from attacking aircraft, and Kip himself was knocked unconscious by the blast concussion. These slavers were thorough and merciless, burning down everyone over the age of seventeen and everyone who resisted. By the end of the day, most of the eight million Scania had been killed and the few thousand children left alive were being herded aboard the slaver starship. During this process, the Anubian Lord Dirac identified Kip as the only potential threat amidst the shocked survivors. Once the starship was in orbit, Kip resisted being put into the slave pens but his attempt to fight back against armored troopers was futile and ended with him receiving a savage beating. Brought before the Slave-Master and Dirac, Kip remained defiant. Amused by this, the Slave-Master decided to personally break his will but before he could be taken away the lights in the corridor went out and an unseen person pulled Kip away from the troopers and into the starship's air ducts. After arriving at one of the slave pens, Kip was surprised to discover that his rescuer was a young woman named Sandy who revealed that the Scania had been the third group captured by the slavers during their current mission. AS Sandy was explaining that their freedom would only last until the slavers reached their base, they heard the battle stations alarm that indicated that the starship was under attack. Once the slaver starship was disabled by Ship, a sentient starship, her partner Star-Lord boarded it and began battling his way through the mercenaries. When that battle came near the slave-pens, a stray energy beam burned an opening in the door, enabling Kip to get his hands on a handheld weapon that had been dropped just outside of the pen and he immediately used the hander to join the fight. Accompanied by some of the other slaves, Kip and Sandy left the slave pen and soon confronted the command crew on their way to the lifeboat bay. A brutal fight broke out, one that ended with all of the slavers dead. Kip and the others were then approached by Star-Lord who revealed that all of the planets that had previously been attacked by the slavers were now uninhabitable and he suggested that Windhölme would be suitable. When Star-Lord stated that he would set up a field of defensive satellites to protect the planet from the slavers, Kip objected, pointing out that satellites were only a temporary solution and that they would only really be safe if whoever was behind the slavers was put out of business. Two days later, Kip and Sandy, who said that she'd stayed with him to keep him out of trouble, met with Star-Lord in the starship's auxiliary bridge where Ship had Kip use his Windrunner abilities to backtrack the starship's course to an alien world orbited by a hundred moons. There, in a floating palace, Kip's mind made contact with the master of that palace but was so repulsed by the evil he sensed within him that he immediately broke contact. Having monitored Kip's trance, Ship was able to identify the world as Cinnibar and the man as Kyras Shakati, a merchant of great renown. After traveling to Cinnibar, Star-Lord, Kip and Sandy used a skimmer to reach Shakati's palace without being detected but were soon confronted by Melyan Constructs, artificial warriors who repaired themselves when damaged. The trio were herded into a trap and suddenly found themselves seemingly back on Windhölme, aboard Kip's family's ship. Kip soon recognized the situation as an encounter with a King Kraken that had occurred a month earlier but this time the Kraken attacked. During the life-or-death battle, the Kraken destroyed the ship and was about to swallow Sandy when Star-Lord was able to see that they were actually trapped in a virtual reality and destroy the Telempathic Crystal that had been projecting it into their minds. The group then confronted Shakati and his aide Arak who had been observing them. Sandy killed Arak when he attacked her and then used his knife to kill Shakati when she realized that he was about to use a hidden blaster implant to kill Star-Lord. While Star-Lord scanned the palace's computer banks for information about the slavers, Kip and Sandy spent some time together, during which Kip revealed that he loved her and they began kissing. kipple.name: Kipple
kipple.origin: Kipple was an Minotaur-like alien from the Andromeda Galaxy who accidentally teleported to a temple on Fautor IV. The people took him as their new god. He used his abilities to keep the belief going and used their offerings to indulge in wine, women and song. This ended when Killpower and his partner Motormouth came to Fautor and Killpower insulted the church by referring to Kipple as a cow. Motormouth and Killpower then teleported to another planet to which Kipple tracked them down and engaged Killpower in battle. Killpower threw a gun with an explosive timing device on it at Kipple. It got caught in one of Kipple's horns and Killpower then punched him back through his teleportation portal to Fautor IV. As he landed back on Fautor, the gun on Kipple's horn exploded and he was killed. The High Priest of Fautor then proclaimed Killpower as their new god.

kirby richards banner.name: Kirby Richards-Banner
kirby richards banner.origin: In the year 2061, Kirby was one of the members of the new Fantastic Four. He and his teammate Enchantress (Vicky Harkness) were attracted to each other. The team was flying the IGSS Fantastic around Earth's new moon, Neoluna, when they encountered hostile Chronometrodes. Kirby could not use his powers to fix the situation because the Chronometrodes were built to target time-travelers. Back on Earth, Valeria Richards-Banner suddenly lost the team's signal. They later reappeared trapped inside one of the Chronometrodes and were rescued by the reunited Fantastic Four.

kiri oshiro.name: Kiri Oshiro
kiri oshiro.origin: Child prodigy Kiri Oshiro was the daughter of Rumiko Fujikawa, a close friend of Technopolis' Baron Tony Stark. Following her parents' death, Tony took Kiri under his wing, and she became his protegee. Unbeknownst to Kiri, Tony himself had been the murderer of her parents, as part of his attempts to cover Technopolis' biggest secret: the airborne disease plaguing the domain that forced all of its inhabitants to wear armor had been orchestrated by Tony's father Howard. Kiri became an inventor, and the head of Mobairu Yōsai Mechaniks. Tony was particularly interested in the internal work of Kiri's armors, and the powerful mainframe that he couldn't get into, so he attempted to absorb Kiri's company to prevent her technology from getting to Technopolis' inhabitants, but he claimed he wanted to acquire the company simply to protect her from his rival and brother Arno Stark. After the death of her boyfriend Peter Urich, who had a secret life as the vigilante known as Spyder-Man, Kiri devoted herself entirely to her work as a way to cope with Peter's death. Kiri's life was put in danger when a spy of Arno infiltrated Kiri's building to investigate her new technologies. After neutralizing the threat with the help of her friend Lila Rhodes, Kiri opened up about her feelings. thumb|left|Kiri's mecha The following day when she was visiting Peter's grave, Technopolis' Grand Marshal Jim Rhodes, who was also Lila's uncle, informed Kiri on a lead on Peter's murderer. Kiri kept working constantly to stay focused, to Lila's dismay. When Jim Rhodes was killed by Tony Stark, the person who had murdered Spyder-Man, Rhodey was able to record and transmit Stark's confession, sending it to Lila. Kiri and Lila then unleashed Kiri's secret weapon, a pair of gigantic suits of armor, to stop the Starks once and for all. A battle of gigantic proportions took place in the streets of Technopolis between the Stark brothers and Kiri and Lila. While Stark revealed the truth to Kiri, she had been using the fight as a misdirection to distract the Starks from a virus she had entered into their suits, and ultimately shut them down. Some time later, the Thors arrived to the scene to take care of the Stark brothers, and dispatched them in the name of Doom. While the inhabitants of Technopolis still suffered of the illness, a process of healing began for Technopolis now that the truth wasn't covered, by the hand of its new Baroness, Kiri Oshiro, accompanied by Technopolis' newly appointed Thor, Lila Rhodes.

kiri shamara.name: Kiri Shamara
kiri shamara.first_appearance: Official Handbook of the Marvel Universe A to Z Update Vol 1 4
kiri shamara.origin: ===Family Legacy=== In 1592, a giant creature named the Wani came from the Ocean off Japan's coast and went on a rampage. It was seen as a sign of the sea god Susanoo's displeasure. The Samurai general Tako Shamara, tainted by the shame of his failures to kill the Wani, stole a Westerner's ship. He used the gunpowder which he found aboard to force the Wani back into the abyss, at the cost of his own life. As the Wani's death was uncertain, the honor of the Shamara family remained tainted. Tako's son Kiri Shamara trained with sorcerers, and that knowledge was passed from a generation to another. The last to wield that powers, named Tako Shamara as well, was killed by KIA, and his own son swore to took up the mantle.

kirigi.name: Kirigi
kirigi.origin: A deadly assassin of The Hand and faithful servant of their then present "Jonin". Kirigi has been said will not die. He survived impalement by his nemesis Elektra and continued to pursue the female assassin after a short recuperation. Elektra next decapitated Kirigi and this seemed to end or severely curtail his existence. However, Kirigi's head and body were reattached and reanimated by the Hand and he returned to attack Daredevil and his allies. This time his body was destroyed by fire which appeared to end his life again. After he fell, agents of Stick destroyed his body.

kirika yashida.name: Kirika Yashida
kirika yashida.origin: In this reality, Weapon X (Logan) and Mariko Yashida had a romance before the ascension of Apocalypse. This romance produced a daughter, whom Mariko named Kirika. Weapon X was unaware of this birth, and following the destruction of Japan joined the X-Men while Mariko joined the Human High Council. Kirika became the property of the evil geneticist Sinister, although the circumstances behind her captivity are presently unrevealed. Following the fall of Apocalypse, Kirika was found in one of Sinister's old labs in a container marked "X-23" by Magneto and the X-Men. Kirika surprised them when she exhibited the ability to extract three bone claws from each hand, making the X-Men realize that she was related to their former comrade. Kirika was invited to join the X-Men, who were now government sanctioned bounty hunters trying to capture all the mutants that aided Apocalypse during his reign. Kirika was trained by Magneto himself, who bonded her skeleton and claws with Adamantium. Magneto sent Kirika out to find Weapon X in Canada and convince him to return to the X-Men. After explaining to him what she knew of her origins and helping Weapon X take down Northstar and Aurora, former minions of Apocalypse, she convinced him to return to America with her. Back in America, Kirika broke up a fight between Weapon X and her uncle the Silver Samurai before the team was called to Washington D.C. to battle Amazon, Cannonball, and Icarus. This proved to be part of a plot to allow their sister Paige to get revenge against the X-Men for leaving her to die during a mission. A battle erupted and all the Guthries were slain. Kirika mortally wounded Paige, Paige revealed to the X-Men that Magneto was secretly preventing Sinister's capture. Kirika listened as Magneto explained that he was blackmailed by Sinister to keep the secret that Jean Grey was responsible for saving the world from nuclear holocaust during Apocalypse's downfall. Kirika joined the X-Men in tracking Sinister to Liberty Island where she clashed with members of his Sinister Six. In the final battle, Sinister was defeated and Kirika aided Weapon X in slaying him by impaling him with their claws. In the aftermath, Kirika had Psylocke use her powers to unlock her memories and learn the truth of her origins. Knowing that she is the biological child of Logan and Mariko, Kirika accompanied the Silver Samurai, Sunfire and Psylocke back to Japan so that she could be reunited with her mother. thumb|right ===Death=== Kirika led Earth-616's X-Force into Apocalypse's citadel to obtain a Life Seed. She was instantly killed by her father, Weapon X, leaving behind a charred corpse.

kirk heinrick.name: Kirk Heinrick
kirk heinrick.origin: Kirk Heinrick was a well known ivory hunter who built a fortress in the Belgian Congo in the early 1940s. Ka-Zar spotted Heinrick's home and investigated. Upon meeting Ka-Zar, Heinrick introduced himself and offered Ka-Zar to work for him by bringing him elephants to slaughter for their ivory. Furious at this request, Ka-Zar attacked Heinrick who quickly gave up. As a show of good faith he suggested Ka-Zar accompany him to his headhunters so he could witness their dismissal. While walking through his compound Heinrick ambushed him and pushed him into an enclosed well. Surrounded by headhunters who were throwing spears at the hero Ka-Zar swam down and discovered a hole in the well that led to the compound's mote and his freedom. Soon after escaping from Heinrick's clutches, Ka-Zar spoke with his friend Trajah who, with his assistance, gathered an army of elephants that stormed Heinrick's home attacking him and his men. The outcome of the battle is left unrevealed, and Heinrick's fate after Ka-Zar's elephant assault is unknown.

kirk lamont.name: Kirk Lamont
kirk lamont.origin: After his failure to build a bridge with innovative techniques that led to the collapse of the bridge itself, the young architect Kirk Lamont was approached by a man named Blane who wanted to hire him to build a floating city in a desert area. Initially skeptical, Lamont had to change his mind when his innovations and the engineering techniques suggested by Blane bore excellent results and a floating city supported only by thin cables was born in the desert. When Blane said that the city was finished, Lamont objected that there were still stairs and elevators to reach the homes, but Blane said that there was no need as his race was able to overcome gravity, and so both Blane and a couple of humanoid aliens that had appeared floated towards the homes taking Lamont with them telling him that he could stay with them. Lamont, however, did not accept and jumped out of the houses telling them that they could not stay on Earth and rushed to call the authorities but when the police went to the place accompanied by Lamont, the city with all the aliens had disappeared. Lamont realized that after this incident he would be expelled from the engineers' society but at the same time he was happy because he had proven that his innovative ideas worked.

kirk marston.name: Kirk Marston
kirk marston.origin: Kirk Marston was a radiologist working for Nayland Smith at MI-6. When Ka-Zar came to London, looking for a cure to a Vibranium-related madness that had befallen the people of the Savage Land, Marston was introduced to him by journalist Tandy Snow. Marston accompanied Snow and Ka-Zar to the Savage Land to inspect the Vibranium. When they arrived, they found that the Savage Land had been invaded by the Sheenarians. After the defeat of the invasion force, Marston accompanied Ka-Zar and Snow to the Sheenarians home dimension. After having fled during a battle with the Quarlians, Marston discovered the Kramen and led Tongah and Bernard Kloss to them. They immunized him to the process of energy absorption to which they then subjected their prisoners. Marston was later captured by Zaladane and subjected to a mystical ritual that transformed him into the host body for Garokk the Petrified Man. Garokk has physically died and been resurrected several times since then, suggesting that the host body of Kirk Marston is effectively dead.

kishi oramosha.origin: Dr. Kishi Oramosha appeared to a philanthropic businessman who provided the funds to build a new science building at University of Tokyo. In actuality he built a doomsday weapon into the building and planned to detonate it to destroy Japan to unite the world under its destruction. He was confronted by Sunfire and the pair fought briefly before Sunfire attacked the building, cutting off its power. Deadline was arrested, claiming this was his real scheme, to unite the youth of Japan to oppose him. He later attacked Big Hero Six and knocked out Sunpyre and was confronted by the Ebon Samurai. After Sunpyre recovered, she and the Samurai were able to capture Deadline.

kistur.name: Kistur
kistur.origin: Kistur was the alien Charles Little Sky stole his Darkhawk armor from. Kistur once tried to kill Little Sky, and Little Sky was forced to shoot him which dislodged Kistur's Darkhawk amulet from his armor and killing him. Little Sky not being able to use this Darkhawk amulet as it was drained of power dumped the amulet in another dimension (Ocsh would later send Darkhawk to retrieve this amulet). Little Sky stole the armor from Kistur's Darkhawk body and took the name Portal and became an ally of Darkhawk. The Mahari Brothers merged Kistur's corpse with two Darkhawk armors to create Overhawk. The two armors were held in storage in Ocsh's ship and at that time did not belong to hosts. Overhawk swore vengeance on Earth and battled Portal and Darkhawk. Kistur and the Mahari Brothers were of warring ethnic groups but from the same planet. Much of Overhawk's origin was rendered moot with the revelation that Chris Powell hallucinated Evilhawk and other Darkhawk armor related characters such as Overhawk and Osch. thumb

kiwi black.name: Kiwi Black
kiwi black.origin: Kiwi Black was a Māori mutant bred by an ancient mutant Azazel, who was trapped in the Brimstone Dimension for thousands of years and was able to visit Earth only for short periods. In order to free himself completely, Azazel sired multiple children across the world. When his children grew up, many of them developed power to teleport into or through the Brimstone Dimension, including Abyss and the X-Men's Nightcrawler. Azazel controlled their minds and forced them all to gather at La Isla des Demonas to perform a ritual that physically connected them all together and combined their powers to open a portal to the Brimstone Dimension big enough for Azazel and his army to return to Earth. Since Kiwi Black wasn't a teleporter and couldn't participate in the ritual, he was instead ordered to guard his half-siblings. Kiwi Black fought against Azazel's mind control, but wasn't able to free himself and was forced to follow orders. The X-Men followed their teammate Nightcrawler to the island, and discovered the ritual. The portal was already half-opened and Azazel and several of his people were already able to pass through. Husk tried to break the circle and free Nightcrawler, but she was attacked by Kiwi Black. Azazel's army meanwhile seemingly killed Iceman with exploding arrows, and attacked Havok with same arrows, eventually causing him to explode. In result the portal's effect was reversed, and instead of bringing Azazel and his army to Earth it brought everyone back to the Brimstone Dimension. Almost all of Azazel's children died during explosion, leaving only Kiwi Black, Nightcrawler and Abyss alive. Kiwi Black and others were brought to Azazel's castle where he revealed to them the truth about being the father of Kiwi Black and two others. Azazel was disappointed what Kiwi hadn't performed his duty well, hadn't stopped the X-Men and ruined his plans, so he allowed Ophis to torture Kiwi. Kiwi Black, however, managed to escape, and instead killed Yidrazil and freed Angel. They wanted to also free Wolverine, who was tortured by Ophis, but the castle was destroyed by Polaris who ripped the dimensional rift in Abyss's body wide apart, allowing the X-Men, Abyss and Kiwi to escape through it and return to Earth, while Azazel and his army were left behind and trapped in the Brimstone Dimension. Kiwi Black then spent some time with his half-brothers in the Xavier's School for Gifted Youngsters. Years later Kiwi Black was among millions of mutants who lost their powers during the M-Day.

kiyoshi kurata.name: Kiyoshi Kurata
kiyoshi kurata.origin: Like his teammates, Kaminari was hired by Rei Takahashi to track down and kill Tony Stark, the man responsible for a nuclear-industry related disaster which financially ruined the Akane Fusion Developments and caused 59 deaths. When James Rhodes presented the evidence linking Stane International and Justin Hammer to the event, Kaminari and the other Masters withdrew from battle. Ashamed of themselves, they offered their services to Stark to reclaim their lost honor. Iron Man, Rhodes, and the Masters all prepared for an assault on Justin Hammer. Kaminari and his teammates attacked Justin Hammer's Villa and defeated the Mandroids, operatives of the Hydra and the Hand, as well as Justin Hammer, who eventually surrendered. The Masters of Silence then immediately disappeared.

kiza.name: Kiza
kiza.origin: At puberty, the mutant gene of the young Japanese girl named Kiza activated, granting her a touch that turned matter into solid gold and skin that burned in contact with oxygen. Her parents were approached by a mysterious man named Lord Yaru, who promised them that he could treat her condition. She was taken into his custody, but he locked her in a one-room cell with a nitrogenous atmosphere and forced her to produce gold for him. Her plight came to the attention of X-Man, who had become mutantkind's "tribal shaman" and dedicated himself to helping mutants in need, wherever they were. Using his massive telekinetic abilities, he freed Kiza from her cell and defeated Lord Yaru and his men, making Yaru swear at his feet to never hurt mutants again. He then showed Kiza the outside world and its beauty for the first time in years of her life, filtering the oxygen from the air around her as he did so. He offered to move her to another planet with an atmosphere than had no oxygen, but she refused, as that meant she would be alone again. Thanking Nate for showing her the world, Kiza turned her golden touch on herself, committing suicide.

kkallakku.name: Kkallakku
kkallakku.origin: ===Origin=== Like each of the Fear Lords, Kkallakku was a mystery, and his origin (or even his very existence) was known to few. The Kkallakku was a Demon that gained his powers from the fear of other lifeforms. He spawned the Kkallakki, better known as the Fear Eaters. ===Modern Age=== The Dweller in Darkness summoned the other members to join him in causing "The Great Fear" and take over Earth. Kkallakku summoned his children, the Fear Eaters, to help with the attack on the planet. The Fear Lords' first area of attack was New York City, feeding off their fears. Doctor Strange intervened and absorbed as much fear from the population as possible. The Fear Eaters were unable to resist Doctor Strange since he hald a city's-worth of fear inside, despite the commands of Kkallakku. Doctor Strange opened a mystical portal to another dimension and jumped through it, luring the Fear Eaters behind him. Once they were in, he jumped back through the portal, back to Earth, trapping the demons in an unnamed dimension. When Kkallakku realized he had lost his artillery force, he fled. Kkallakku later met with the other Fear Lords to discuss the Serpent's attempted conquest of Earth and the group was gathered again by Kid Loki to stop Nightmare from becoming the King of Fear by forging the Serpent's fear into a crown and usurping all the other Lords' power. To this end they were tricked into a stalemate where none could possess the crown without it being taken by another. This seemingly lasted until Mephisto claimed the crown for himself and the Fear Lords bent to his will, feeding off the fear Mephisto gave them from the crown. It is presumed that when Kid Loki sacrificed himself the crown faded and the Fear Lords left Mephisto's service.

klagg.name: Klagg
klagg.origin: Klagg is a peaceful alien from an unknown planet. Klagg is an alien inside a powerful robotic suit of armor which is also his starship. This ship resembles a 7 foot tall humanoid robot. Whilst lost in this sector of the galaxy, Klagg landed on Earth to get his bearings, and was surprised to find the planet inhabited. Klagg demonstrated the power of his ship to Earth’s leaders. When he learned that the humans of Earth still indulged in petty wars. Klagg decides that it is his duty to destroy Earth's civilization before man's war like nature spreads to the rest of the Universe. Klagg starts to attack the natives, until all nations of the world banded together against Klagg. Seeing man's unity against him as a sign of hope that mankind may not be all savages. Klagg decides maybe man could work together for peace and progress and the leaves the Earth. At some point, the Fantastic Four captured Klagg back on Earth and transported him to Monster Isle. Klagg later teamed up with many other monsters and many other superhumans. They all had one goal, protecting their home planet from a violent invading force of monsters.

klara prast.name: Klara Prast
klara prast.origin: ===Origin=== Klara Prast was born in Bern, Switzerland where she was raised by a devoutly religious mother on a farm. When Klara first started speaking to plants, she assumed it was something everyone did. However, her mother was convinced Klara's mutant power was witchcraft and arranged for her to be married to the much older, Mr. Prast, who was departing for the United States. left|200px|thumb|Klara being threatened by Mr. Prast (Earth-616)|her husband In New York City, Prast forced Klara to work and suppress her powers. He regularly drank heavily, and was physically, verbally, and sexually abusive to Klara. left|150px|thumb|Klara deciding to travel to the future with the Runaways (Earth-616)|Runaways ===Runaways=== Klara was working in a sweatshop on the Lower East Side when a fire broke out. Luckily, the Runaways, who had accidentally traveled back in time, were there to rescue the workers from the fire. Klara was able to escape using her botanopathy, but not before being spotted by Karolina Dean. Karolina saw Klara again later by accident while she was being threatened by her husband. The next day Karolina and Molly purposely found Klara, and Molly offered her a spot on the team. However, when Klara saw Karolina and Xavin kissing, she became frightened and ran away. This was due to both being apparently female and the strong religious teachings against homosexuality common at that time. Klara later decided to depart with the Runaways after another beating from Prast. right|200px|thumb|Klara finding peace in the future After traveling to the present, the Runaways decided to remain in New York for a few days to allow Klara to acclimate to the future and say goodbye to the city. Unfortunately, this was during the beginning of the Skrulls invasion of Earth. Xavin and the other Runaways were caught in the fighting alongside the Young Avengers, but Speed was able to carry Molly and Klara to safety at Mount Rushmore. When the Runaways finally returned to California, the group took up residence in one of the Pride's safehouses, the Malibu House. Unfortunately, they were soon attacked by the Light Brigade. The Light Brigade were survivors of the destruction of Majesdane, Karolina's parents' homeworld, and they blamed Karolina for the destruction and demanded that she return with them to face trial for her actions. In a bid to get rid of them, Nico cast the spell "Scatter", which sent the four members of the Light Brigade to different corners of the Earth. klarkash ton.name: Klarkash-Ton
klarkash ton.origin: Klarkash-Ton was an aged Atlantean priest, who recounted the creation of the strange kingdoms on the far-western continent, such as Poseidonis, Zothique, and Mayapan, as well as possibly their visit by Conan (see notes).

fields.history: Klarkash-Ton was an aged Atlantean priest, who recounted the creation of the strange kingdoms on the far-western continent, such as Poseidonis, Zothique, and Mayapan, as well as possibly their visit by Conan (see notes).
fields.notes: Klarkash-Ton was created in ( ; August, 1931) by H.P. Lovecraft, as a tip of the hat to Clark Ashton Smith (friend, correspondent, and creator of concepts such as Tsathoggua or the Commoriom myth-cycle, mentioned in the story). The only in-universe reference to Clark Ashton Smith is a book by a or about "Clarkashton" (seen in "Tales of the Zombie!: Damballah's Deeds", in ; December, 1982). It is possibly a reference to Klarkash-Ton. In the last section of the final chapter of the Conan Comics Chronology ( ; February, 1995), Roy Thomas mentioned that the revelations of Klarkash-Ton were supposed to be unveiled in the following issues of . The title was cancelled after (July, 1995) without any stories fitting the description, and it is possible that the stories planned were never produced. Similarly, the story "Requiem for a Conqueror", mentioned in the same section to be released soon in Savage Sword of Conan, was never published. The title was launched to replace Savage Sword. Though it was cancelled as well, its last issue, (May, 1996), was an adaptation of Smith's story "Necromancy in Naat" (1936), set on the Isle of Na'at and mentioning Mayapan and Zothique, but no mention of Klarkash-Ton was found. This story might the result of the stories teased in the Conan Comics Chronology. It should also be noted that included stories adapted from stories by Clark Ashton Smith, and the whole volume story-line revolved around Tolometh, the ancient god of Poseidonis (mentioned in ; June, 1995). It is possible that Roy Thomas was only mirroring Lovecraft's own pun, and mentioning stories possibly adapted from Smith's stories, without intent of mentioning or depicting Klarkash-Ton in the mentioned stories. The exact scope of those revelations is unclear whether they only mention the strange kingdoms of the far-western continent, or if they include Conan's visits. Similarly, the temporal setting of Klarkash-Ton remains unclear (whether he was alive during the Pre-Cataclysmic Age and survived, or was of one of the Atlantean settlements of the Great Cataclysm).

klaus.name: Klaus
klaus.origin: Klaus was a member of the Thule Society who participated in the blitzkrieg on Washington, D.C. piloting a Mech paired with Erich. After Veil rescued a woman from under some rubble, as soon as she was rescued, she was killed by a volley of bullets from Klaus' Mech. This enraged Veil who killed Klaus and Erich by suffocating them. ; In the continuation of the blitz, when another the two pilots of another Mech found Veil entering their cabin in gaseous form, remembering how she had killed Klaus and Erich they tried to escape in flight but to no avail.

klaus erskine.name: Klaus Erskine
klaus erskine.origin: In September 1935, he attempted to flee Germany with his family. His grandfather, on his mother's side, was a Jew and Abraham Erskine wanted to take his family to safety. They were stopped at the Germany/Switzerland border by Johann Schmidt and his men. Schmidt wanted Erskine's work on ways to increase molecular density of cellular fibers through synthetic proteins. In order to ensure Abraham's cooperation, Schmidt sent him, his mother Greta, and his sister Marlene to the Dachau concentration camp. He died during a typhus outbreak.

klaus kruptmann.name: Klaus Kruptmann
klaus kruptmann.first_appearance: All This and World War II
klaus kruptmann.origin: Dr. Klaus Kruptmann was a loyal Nazi scientist working in top secret research projects for the Nazi High Command during the World War Two. In 1943, Kruptmann was assigned to Baron Heinrich Zemo's research team. The team aimed to understand and reproduce an alien ship that had crashlanded in Berlin, killing all of its occupants. In a matter of months, Zemo and his lackeys had repaired the Orphu ship and discovered that it was an Orphu Time Machine. They also built two more operative time machines upon the original design. The Red Skull then decided to send three elite teams, the Blautot Commandos, to the future, with orders of obtaining futuristic weaponry to be used in the war. The teams were sent to 5718, 2146 and 1989. The 5718 team was lost and the 2146 brought an important, futuristic weapon. At this point, however, Kruptmann was ordered to abandon this project. Kruptmann then worked in other projects for the Nazis, until the defeat of Germany in 1945. He then was one of the subjects of Operation Paperclip or a similar project. The Americans wanted to use his scientific expertise (and avoid the Soviets using it), so they eagerly accepted Kruptmann in the United States. Kruptmann began working in secret projects for the American people, although he still retained his former Nazi loyalties. He longed to restore the glory of the Third Reich, and contributed with Nazi-backed South American crime unions. In 1989, Kruptmann was working in a "chronal displacement" project for the federal government, under the orders of former Allied officer Nick Fury. Fury appreciated and trusted Kruptmann because he was one of the few living people he knew who remembered the war. The scientist in the next lab was Dr. Jack Cooper, who was working on the Cavalier Infantry Support System, a hulking tank-like robot. Kruptmann noticed that the 1989 unit of the Blautot Commandos would appear near San Diego. Kruptmann greets the commandos and offered his home as HQ. He also provided them with access to the secret facility in Albuquerque he was working in with a microscanner, and information about the Cavalier project. Kruptmann did not know that Fury had called some super-heroes to test the Cavalier. The Blautot Commandos tried to get hold of the robot but were defeated by the heroes. Although the Commandos were trained for questioning and did not reveal Kruptmann's name, Kruptmann was nevertheless discovered because of the missing microscanner. He panicked and tried to attack the heroes with an experimental laser rifle, but was defeated and captured. Base security guards took him to jail.

klaus voorhees.origin: thumb|left|Klaus Voorhees ===Origin=== Klaus Voorhees was an ex-convict working with the humanitarian medical researcher Professor Ezekiel Shecktor in India on a universal antitoxin for snake venom. Jealous of Shecktor's success, Voorhees plotted to kill him and make the murder look like an accident. Hence, Voorhees induced one of the cobras kept in the laboratory to bite both Shecktor and himself. Voorhees planned to use the universal antitoxin to save himself from death. Unknown to Voorhees, the cobra had been irradiated. The combination of the radioactive venom in his bloodstream and the experimental anti-toxin which he used created a mutagenic catalyst which gave Voorhees certain cobra-like powers. ===Thor=== Assuming the costumed guise of the Cobra, Voorhees used his new found superhuman abilities for crime. Cobra travelled back to the United States, initially defeating Thor in their first encounter but Thor escaped after returning to Don Blake. The Cobra then went to the offices of Dr. Bruce Andrews and kidnapped Jane Foster climbing out of the window. Assuming he defeated Thor, he let his guard down which allowed Thor to strike. Cobra dropped Jane and escaped as Thor saved her life. ===Teaming Up with Mr. Hyde=== Cobra began his long time partnership with another of Thor's adversaries, Mister Hyde. But the team of the Cobra and Mister Hyde were defeated repeatedly, first by Thor and later by the costumed crime fighter Daredevil. Hyde and Cobra were among the many costumed menaces assembled by Doctor Doom to disrupt the wedding of Reed Richards and Susan Storm. Hyde and the Cobra next battled Daredevil. He then teamed with the original Jester and Mr. Hyde against Daredevil. Teaming with the Mr. Hyde again, Cobra attempted to acquire Cagliostro's serum. He was next employed by the Purple Man, and battled Daredevil in an arena alongside Mr. Hyde, the Jester, and the Gladiator. ===Serpent Squad=== Cobra served as a lead of the Serpent Squad with the Eel and the first Viper (Jordan Dixon). With the Serpent Squad, he attacked Captain America and the Falcon. He subsequently joined the second Serpent Squad led by Viper (Madame Hydra) after Jordan Dixon's death. They battled Steve Rogers in his "Nomad" identity, and then became involved in an attempt to raise the continent of Lemuria. He became trapped with the second Viper, and his cowardice earned her enmity. ===The Raft=== The Cobra came to believe that his criminal career would fare more successfully if he no longer acted in partnership with Hyde. The hired mercenaries were each a component of a bomb designed to destroy the city. Fury and his team were able to stop them and arrested them all including Cobra. ===Thunderbolts=== After the Superhuman Registration Act passed, Cobra was forced to join the Thunderbolts and was trained by Swordsman (Andreas Strucker), along with the Unicorn and the Enforcer Ox. However they later rebelled and Cobra along with Mauler, Firebrand, and Mr. Hyde and attacked Yellowjacket, Constrictor, and other Initiative staff and trainees at Camp Hammond. ===X-Men=== Cobra and the Serpent Society were among the many villains the X-Men took down while protecting San Francisco. They were robbing a bank until they were defeated by Hope Summers. ===Transforming his Nephew=== Upon becoming King Cobra, Klaus passed the Cobra identity on to his nephew Piet Voorhees, administering the same mutagenic compound that gave him his powers. ===Brief retirement=== It was mentioned that Klaus had retired as King Cobra. That lasted until Dario Agger persuaded him to come out of retirement and spring Mister Hyde from Ravencroft. They worked with Grey Gargoyle and Radioactive Man (who claimed to the police that he's still with the Thunderbolts) in attacking Thor. The first time had the villains retreating because of Enchantress. By the next fight, the foursome were defeated by Thor, Enchantress, Sif, and Magni and remanded to Daedalus LLC which turned out to be a subsidiary of Roxxon.

klaxon.name: Klaxon
klaxon.origin: Klaxon was a bounty hunter from Ubliex, a planet that no ship could escape because of how close it was to the black hole Singularity 105-6B. Mere days before the planet was to be swallowed completely, he was hired by the Brotherhood of Badoon to retrieve the drug runner L'Wit, revealed to be the last living heir to the Badoon throne. With time of the essence, Klaxon wasted no time finding L'Wit and simply had her find him instead by hiring her to deliver a shipment to him. After Klaxon confirmed that he had the target, the Badoon revealed that his payment was only the way off the dying planet: the Elemental, an item of great power that could only be used once and could charge a starship enough escape the black hole's gravity. The Elemental was dropped off on Ubliex by a drone, but was stolen by the Vestigials. Eventually Gamora took control of the Vestigials' ship and offered L'Wit and a few others to escape the dying Ubliex along with her. Klaxon was one of them, piloting a ship beyond the black hole's gravitational pull. Afterwards, Gamora departed them to return to Thanos, leaving the survivors to find their own way.

klee varr.name: Klee-Varr
klee varr.origin: Klee-Varr was a citizen of the Utopian Kree Faction who lived with his family in the colony planet of Elysion-3. One day, Klee-Varr's son had a prophetic nightmare of the planet being destroyed, but Klee-Varr and his wife brushed it off. After heading to work and meeting up with a coworker, Klee-Varr witnessed the sudden arrival of New Olympus. The Olympians ravaged the planet, presumably killing Klee-Varr in the process, while his son was turned by Hephaestus into one of his automatons.

kleezar.origin: In 1948 the Earth was threatened by the Jovians who began using their Ray of Madness on the Earth. The Torch was able to carry out the seemingly impossible task of flying to Jupiter under his own power and slaying the Jovians and their leader Kleezar, saving the Earth.

klobok.name: Klobok
klobok.origin: Klobok was a Skrull who began to research the mystical origins of the Dire Wraiths, who were an offshoot of the Skrull race. His pursuit of arcane knowledge was frowned upon by the Superskrulls of the Science Caste and he was sentenced to hard labor on an off-world penal colony. This punishment meant he survived Galactus' destruction of the Skrull homeworld. When the Annihilation Wave began, the colony was destroyed allowing Klobok to escape. He once again took up his research, and in the process conjured up the deceased Dire Wraith Warlock Doctor Dredd. From him, he learned the arcane secrets of the Wraiths and actually assumed the identity of Dredd. Feeling science had failed his people, he set out to find a way to save the Skrulls from extinction through Dire Wraith Sorcery. He formulated a plan whereby he could insinuate the Dire Wraith Queen Volx into the retinue of the Galadorian Queen Brandy Clark and manipulate her. Using information gained from this source and from his infiltration of a Rigellian Survey ship, Koblok - as Dredd - attacked the Galadorian stronghold known as The Keep which guarded access to the dreaded Dark Nebula. With the knowledge gained from the Rigellians to 'cut' space and relocate the Black Sun from the cloak inside the nebula to the Galadorian system. The two stellar masses began to merge with the Black Sun consuming the Galadorian sun when the Annihilators intervened. They also were forced to return Wraithworld from Limbo to balance the solar system which played into Klobok's plan. Klobok then revealed himself and began a massive conjuration to disassemble the Dire Wraiths and revert their DNA back to create a new race of Skrulls and re-establish the Skrull Empire. The Annihilators fought the assembled Hellhounds, Deathwings, and Watchwraiths that Koblok summoned and kept him busy until Volx moved into position where she tongue-spiked Koblok and dragged him to his doom, thereby saving the Dire Wraiths.

klrr.origin: When Galactus begun consuming the Skrull's Throneworld, the Skrull known as Klrr saw his father die, while his mother got Klrr to a ship in order to ensure his survival, sacrificing herself in the process. thumb|left|Human form Klrr grew to become a loyal agent to the Skrull Empire, and selected to breed with the Skrull, G'iah and conceive children, since G'iah was from Skrull a planet whose offspring had becomeWarskrulls, and the two even fell in love. Their mission was to infiltrate Human society, and pave the way for a future invasion of Earth. They raised their three daughters on Earth, under the guise of a typical family. However, during one mission, their youngest daughter had been captured, thought murdered, by Project Blossom who sought to exterminate all of the infiltrated Skrulls. The family kept continuing their mission, gathering information, while posing as humans and working in their human identities. At some point Klrr was informed by another fellow Skrull agent, Moloth, an agent of Project Blossom had been killing entire Skrull groups. While almost all of the family were doing their mission, with Klrr and G'iah impersonating Tony Stark and Pepper Potts and stealing information, Alice faced the agent who had come to their house in order to kill them, but after the struggle Alice killed him instead. Klrr was gleeful at this, since he could now pose as the agent and infiltrate more easily, and was proud of his daughter, but his wife was disgusted on what their family had become and beat Klrr. After that, they begun their subsequent mission which was retrieving a thing which allowed Project Blossom to locate the Skrulls. Klrr in guise of the agent went to a part of the facility, while the rest in another part, since their objective was behind a door which could open by turning two keys in those places. Upon opening the door G'iah was shocked to find their long lost daughter behind the door and whose blood was being used for detecting Skrulls. After rescuing their daughter and exiting the facility, Klrr was greeted by Moloth who then killed Klrr, having betrayed the Skrull Empire and joined Project Blossom. His body was then recovered by a grieving Alice.

kludge.name: Kludge
kludge.species: Human with latent Inhuman lineageCategory:Human/Inhuman HybridsCategory:Hybrids activated by the Terrigen Bomb
kludge.origin: Kludge used to be a contract carpenter and mechanic who worked on and tinkered with machinery before the Terrigen Mist cloud resulting from the Terrigen Bomb hit and affected him due to his Inhuman heritage. Exposure to the mist's left him mentally impaired and vulnerable to manipulation, which was right around the time former actor turned Nuhuman crime boss Ajay found and opted him to build a specially designed control hub for diverting and manipulating Mumbai's electrical grid attack, then sent him to attack a national naval destroyer in a ploy to lure out the Inhuman International Envoy, particularly Grid as the former had use for his electromagnetic powers, constructing a battle suit composed various mechanical components, parts of which belonging to the very fleet ship he was taking apart. He was untimely stopped by the arrival of the Inhumans when hit by a powerful electromagnetic pulse which fried all of his suits' systems. He was taken into the custody of Crystal at the behest of the Indian government and imprisoned within the R.I.V..

klug.name: Klug
klug.origin: The man known as Klug was born hideously deformed. In 1935, he killed a group of men who made fun of his appearance, an act that landed him on death row and to the electric chair. Somehow surviving, Klug went into seclusion and began developing a massive electrical generator hidden in a cave that charged specially made lightning guns so that he could slay those responsible for sending him to the chair. With the help of his minions, Klug began using his lightning generator to strike the homes of the law officials who were responsible for sending him away. The strange killings attracted the attention of both the Sub-Mariner and Betty Dean. After saving the life of the Governor of New England, Namor triangulated the source of the attacks but was struck down with a bolt of lightning himself. Klug then kidnapped Betty and told her his origins. Deciding that Betty should be his wife, he then hooked her up to his electrical generator, telling her the electricity would deform her and make her uglier than he was. Having survived the electrical jolt, Namor destroyed the hydro-generator that powered Klug's device and defeated his men. Getting hold of an electrical pistol, Namor confronted Klug to a duel. Namor ultimately one, one of his electrical jolts sending Klug falling seemingly to his death. In the aftermath of the battle, Betty noted that Klug was wearing a rubber suit and might still be alive. Namor dismissed this notion and returned to the ocean. As Klug has not been seen since, it is presumable that he is indeed dead.

kluh.name: Kluh
kluh.species: Clone of a human gamma ray mutate
kluh.origin: The Kluh is an intelligent incarnation of the Grey Hulk, a "superior" clone created by Xemnu in a failed attempt to destroy the Hulk and replace his very absence with Kluh. Kluh and Xemnu also had to fight Red Hulk up to the point where Impossible Man, who was watching the fight, used his Valizian Compounder to merge both Hulks into the Compound Hulk. Kluh was apparently killed by the Compound Hulk when this plan fell apart.

knight america.name: Knight America
knight america.origin: The Second Dark Age arose from the fires of the Atomic Age and the aftermath of the Second World War. What once was the danger of "mutual assured destruction" became the unraveling of the Second Industrial Revolution. With the world's nations broken and technology lost, darkness not only covered the world, but also consumed the hearts of many who remained. Those with evil intent began to build their own kingdoms by corrupting the willing and enslaving the weak. All hope seemed lost for centuries until The Sentinel of Liberty, Knight America, fought back against these tyrant kings. Following the traditions of a bygone era, Knight America would gather anyone, willing to listen, around the bonfires to hear the ancient oral tales of loyalty, selflessness and the magnification of moral fiber. Armed with only his shield and sword, and the full plate mail which he adorned, Knight America set out to encourage and rally the people to work together and push back against the darkness to bring about a new age of hope and hearth fire for all people.

knobby.name: Knobby
knobby.origin: Knobby was a living marionette that resided in the potentially imaginary realm of Nowhere in the Land of Fairy's. Before given life, he was once a ordinary wooden club, and sometimes longed for his old existence. At some point he became a prisoner of the evil magician known as Zar. Knobby was eventually rescued by Jimmy Jupiter and he helped Jimmy defeat the evil wizard and escape his castle. Becoming fast friends with Jimmy, Knobby agreed to help Jimmy find the castle of King Ra . Their travels led to many dangers, and Knobby helped Jimmy escape them, such as when they encountered the Three Witches and their magic pair of glasses, which Jimmy took from them . Knobby later fell down a pit, and Jimmy used these glasses to command snakes to make a rope for Knobby to climb out of. They also passed through the Haunted Forest, when Knobby realized the glasses were influencing Jimmy until they were removed by knights of King Ra upon their arrival outside the castle walls . Finally meeting the King, Knobby joined Jimmy and Fairy Delight on a tour of the Land of Fairey's and visited many of its lands. When they were in the Land of Dreams, Knobby and the others fled the Sandman trying to avoid being put to eternal sleep. Jimmy ended up being returned to Earth, leaving Knobby's fate unknown .

knud.name: Knud
knud.origin: Knud was the chieftain of the Marauders, a Norse tribe which invaded the land of Jarl Olaf. As part of an alternative plan to conquer his enemy, Knud enlisted the help of dwarves from Nidavellir. The dwarves mined out a magical gem, which Knud used to transfer his soul into Olaf's body, leaving his former body lifeless. Under the grounds that Knud had died, "Olaf" called a truce and ordered his land to be shared between his people and the Marauders. Unwilling to allow the dwarves to have the opportunity to let someone else have the power he possessed, Knud told on the dwarves that had helped him, and they were arrested by their superiors.

knull.name: Knull
knull.species: Elder God; Primordial deity of the Abyss
knull.origin: ===Origins=== Knull was an ancient, malevolent deity who purportedly ruled over the Abyss, the existential chasm that existed between the destruction of the Sixth Cosmos and the creation of the Seventh Cosmos. While Knull drew his power from and claimed to be the incarnation of the primordial darkness, it existed long before even him. thumb|left|Attacking a Celestial after they had offered him the position of the King in Black Originally content to slumber in the Void, Knull was awakened when the Celestials began creating the universe. The Celestials recruited Knull to be the King in Black, a cosmic caretaker for the new universe. However, Knull rejected the King in Black's responsibilities and lashed out. Outraged that his kingdom of darkness was being despoiled, Knull created a sword of living darkness from his newly-cast shadow and decapitated one of them. Cast back into the void by the other Celestials, Knull used the slain Celestial's severed head as a forge to temper his sword in its cosmic energies, thus forging All-Black the Necrosword. Intent on reclaiming his kingdom of darkness, Knull manifested a symbiotic suit of armor from the eldritch darkness he commanded and embarked on a genocidal campaign against the other gods and life itself, becoming a legendary figure of terror for divine beings even billions of years later. Unknown to Knull, he and All-Black were linked to the headless body of the Celestial he had killed, something that amplified the power of both the primordial god of darkness and the weapon. In response to Knull's threat, the Celestials created a god of light to oppose him, known as the Enigma Force. ===Symbiote Hive=== ====Reign of Terror==== Hellbent on returning the cosmos to the Abyss, Knull created an artificial planet from the living abyss he controlled to serve as his throneworld and base of operations. Experimenting with his ability to manifest life out of darkness itself, Knull began using the Exoteric Latitude as a dumping ground for his failed creations, which millennia later became known as the Exolon. Among his early creations were proto-symbiotes such as Mister E, and a horde of wyvern-like monsters. Establishing himself as the divine nexus of the abyssal entities' hive-mind, Knull sent them forth into the cosmos -- using them to conquer countless planets, devour civilizations and pantheons, extinguish stars, and smother entire planets in eldritch darkness. The few gods that Knull spared were forcibly drafted into his army, enslaved to his will and transformed into monsters using the living abyss, placed as sentries to guard the worlds he had conquered. thumb|right|God-Host of the symbiote hive At some point during Knull's war against the Light, he encountered the time-displaced Silver Surfer when the former Herald of Galactus freed a world from Knull's control using the Power Cosmic. After a brief but intense fight, Knull defeated the Silver Surfer and infected him with living abyss to turn him into the Void Knight. However, the Silver Surfer was freed by Ego the Living Planet, who helped Radd escape when Knull pursued him on a symbiote dragon. Knull hunted the Silver Surfer down and dueled him, intent on reclaiming him for his army. Knull nearly succeeded in doing so, but was defeated when the Silver Surfer expended the last of his Power Cosmic to conjure a star right in front of him, bathing him in stellar plasma and blasting him across the cosmos. This defeat proved temporary, as Knull recovered and resumed his conquest of the cosmos. thumb|left|Fighting a god empowered by the Enigma Force At some point afterward, Knull engaged an army of gold-armored gods empowered by the Enigma Force in combat and slaughtered all but one golden knight, who received the full concentration of the Light. Pursuing the survivor, Knull managed to impale him on All-Black but was himself impaled through the head by the enemy god's spear, All-Light. Knull and the dying god crash-landed on a desolate planet, where All-Black left the incapacitated Knull for one of the indigenous inhabitants, Gorr. Despite this setback, Knull chose to not hunt the thief down and reclaim All-Black, though he remained aware of Gorr unwittingly following in his footsteps as the God Butcher. After recovering from his injuries over the course of a century, Knull began experimenting with his powers and discovered that he could manifest amorphous parasites called symbiotes from the living abyss and bond them to lesser life forms, corrupting life rather than eradicating it. ====Downfall==== Knull's reign of terror came to an end in the sixth century CE, when two symbiote dragonsone black and one red—arrived on Earth and were named the Grendel and Grendel's Mother by the Danes. The Grendel's rampage was stopped by Thor, who blasted it with divine lightning and severed Knull's connection to the vast majority of symbiotes. As the symbiotes bonded to benevolent hosts, the hive-mind became tainted with notions of honor

fields.personality: As the King in Black, Knull was supposed to keep maintenance over the Celestials' creations, but he refused the work. Knull despises the Celestials and their creations, attempting to carry out a genocide against them by corrupting and slaughtering all life. Revelling in bloodshed and destruction, Knull often sports a predatory grin when engaged in combat and fondly reminisced to Eddie Brock about the devastation he and All-Black had wrought together. He is also arrogant and sadistic—regarding his conquest of the universe as being inevitable, mocking the Silver Surfer's attempt to fight him or escape as futile, and relishing the prospect of hunting the fleeing Surfer down and either killing him or corrupting him. Knull's hubris is one of his greatest weaknesses, as he routinely underestimates opponents he sees as beneath himself—such as the Silver Surfer, Venom, and Thor—and rarely fights using the full extent of his own power, instead opting to let his symbiotes do the fighting for him. Through his symbiote army, Knull is responsible for the destruction and corruption of entire civilizations across the universe. When not engaged in combat, Knull appeared calm and condescending, often smiling in a sadistic fashion at sights such as Venom's berserk form, which he called beautiful. However, Knull possesses a volatile temper and is prone to reacting with extreme rage when denied what he wants, such as when Eddie tried to stop him from re-corrupting the Venom symbiote or when the Silver Surfer refused to serve him. Knull was begrudgingly impressed by Eddie's determination to understand the eldritch truth behind the symbiotes' origins, but mocked him for being deceived by the symbiotes' hive-mind. He considers the symbiotes who rebelled against and imprisoned him to be cowards, liars, and traitors, sneering at their desperate efforts to cover up their dark origins and keep themselves from relapsing. Despite his loathing respect for them—seeing them as his wayward children—he hates the Klyntar symbiotes for betraying him and eventually forcibly absorbed them back into his dark hive-mind.

transportation: In addition to using symbiote dragons as mounts, Knull is capable of manifesting draconic wings from his symbiote for flight.
fields.notes: According to Donny Cates, takes place before Knull lost All-Black. However, during his battle against the Silver Surfer, Knull summoned his symbiotes to aid him, which contradicts elements of his story, since established that Knull created the symbiotes after losing All-Black. Knull's spiral emblem is based on the Spiral of Carcosa from , and is a reference to the Cthulhu Mythos. Similarly, his title of the "King in Black" is a reference to Hastur, the and ruler of Carcosa. The spiral may have also been partly influenced by 's works. Upon learning of him from Spider-Man, Bruce Banner theorized that Knull was merely an aspect of the One Below All or a creature it somehow controls, something that is supported by Doctor Strange's own theory about the Anti-All, a creature born from the Below-Place and possibly tied with the One Below All that, when being shattered by the Lifebringer One, would give birth to the other dark entities in the next Multiverses, including Knull. The One Below All is himself possibly inspired by the Cthulhu Mythos, as is Knull. When asked if the Anti-All was the progenitor of Knull, Al Ewing responded that he would rather leave such matters up to another writer in comic form than provide a boring answer in an interview. While Scorn stated that Knull had resurrected Cletus Kasady as a newborn when he died of nuchal cord strangulation, marking him as an agent of the Void, this was fabricated by the Cult of Knull in order to sensationalize Kasady as Knull's chosen one. The foreword to claims that Knull was from the era of the First Firmament; however, the official timeline at the end of and the recap at the start of identify Knull's Abyss as the existential chasm that was between the destruction of the previous Sixth Cosmos and the creation of the current Seventh/Eighth Cosmos. According to Knull himself, he is "as old as the universe" (though he is technically slightly older), reinforcing the idea that he was spawned in the void before the current universe. Hela made the distinction between Knull and Oblivion. Knull is merely of the void, whereas Oblivion is the void. Oblivion is what Knull wishes to be.
fields.trivia: According to Donny Cates, Knull was the first "something" in the universe. When asked what Knull would have done had he encountered Carnage or one of Venom's other offspring, Ryan Stegman replied that he would have "either [tried] to hurt them or re-consume them and bring them back to Klyntar." According to Jordan D. White, Knull almost never uses his immense full power out of contempt towards his opponents, seeing mortals like humans as being mere insects. Additionally, at the time of Queen in Black he was still in the process of mastering his new God of Light powers and thus unable to use them to their full potential. Several beings have—deliberately or unintentionally—emulated Knull: Almost all of the Nameless Kree infected by the Exolon develop a physical resemblance to Knull—possessing pale skin, long white hair, and an emaciated physique. Gorr the God Butcher, Old Galactus, Ego the Living Planet, and King Loki all attempted to use the All-Black symbiote into continuing Knull's crusade to annihilate all of existence. When Spider-Man bonded to the symbiote, it formed mirrored white spider emblems on its chest and back, which Spider-Man assumed was inspired by Spider-Woman's costume. In reality, the symbiote unconsciously formed the white spider emblems in emulation of Knull's red dragon emblem. Malekith the Accursed learned of Knull by reading the mind of the Venom symbiote, and sought to turn it into his own version of All-Black, wielding it as a dagger and sword during the War of the Realms. After assimilating the Venom symbiote, Dark Carnage was transformed into an even more powerful form sporting draconic wings and horns and pauldrons and arm-wraps resembling Knull's. During his invasion of Earth, most of the people infected by symbiotes resembled Knull. Knull's history, and those of his successors as wielders of All-Black the Necrosword, are recorded in a self-writing divine tome called the Saga of the God Butcher. When asked if King Thanos had managed to kill Knull in the future where he succeeded in killing everything, Donny Cates stated that he had not due to Knull being unkillable, later elaborating that Knull was probably happy to reclaim his kingdom of darkness from the ruins that King Thanos had left in his wake. However, Knull in the 616 timeline did legitimately die at the end of and had to be resurrected in . appeared to tease Knull's survival as his living abyss was seen growing on the sun's surface, but it was likely dropped after Cates left the title. Ryan Stegman's concept art for Knull depicts him with a cape rather than a waistcloth, and questions whether or not he should have eyes and hair.

knut caine.name: Knut Caine
knut caine.species: Human mystically enhanced by a magic dagger provided by Loki
knut caine.origin: Knut Caine, also called the Mad Viking, was a terrorist that terrorized the city of Oslo, Norway until he was captured, but he claimed that he was above the laws of humans because he was the spiritual descendant of Loki. He later escaped prison and tortured the judge at presided over his trial as well as the judge's wife. He then fled into an area with fjords while being pursued by Hank and the Wasp. After entering a cavern, he was approached by the spirit of Loki who had been watching Caine and gave him a magic dagger that contained Loki's power. Caine plunged the dagger into his heart and was transformed into a superhuman form. After fighting off Pym and Wasp, he used his power to create a palace for himself filled with women he captured. Pym and Wasp challenged Caine again while aided by the Hulk. The Hulk was able to kill Caine by forcing a snake Caine transformed into a replica of Midgard Serpent bite him. The serpent's venom was potent enough that it was fatal to Caine, and he died, causing everything he transformed with his magic to revert to normal.

ko bin su.origin: Ko Bin Su is Department H's Chief Engineer. He helped to develop Heather Hudson's geothermal battle suit, as well as developing the semi-organic synthoid duplicates of the Master. He was also responsible for Department H's training/mock battle area known as Combat Centrale. Ko Bin Su is reportedly from Korea. He fled the political instabilities that plagued his Korean family, and made a new life for himself. He is secretly guilty of many indiscretions.

ko rel.name: Ko-Rel
ko rel.species: Kree given part of the Nova Force
ko rel.origin: A captain in the Kree military, Ko-Rel fought against the Annihilation Wave alongside her crew until their cruiser was shot down and crashed on the planet Drez-Lar. She lead the surviving members for a year, sending out a help message everyday, hoping for rescue. Arriving in Kree space as the Phalanx sealed it off, Nova (Richard Rider) was forced into a retreat, hitting the barrier erected by the Phalanx at maximum velocity and falling onto the surface of Drez-Lar, nearly dead. He was quickly found by Ko-Rel on a routine patrol, causing the Xandarian Worldmind to imbue her with part of its power, so as to have an active representative to help Rider, who housed the Worldmind's essence. Taking the weakened Rider back to her ship after the Worldmind had insisted, she left him there to recover until the Phalanx, led by Gamora, attacked the ship, looking for him. Wanting to lead the Phalanx away from her crew, she fled the fight, taunting the Phalanx into following her. She then began battling them in the air above the ship, not aware of Gamora sneaking through the ship, killing members of her crew and eventually finding Rider, who she assimilated into the Phalanx. When she was finished fighting the Phalanx, Ko-Rel was shocked to find that she failed the people she promised to protect. The Worldmind that called her, asking her to kill Rider and himself before he succumbs to the transmode virus; the Phalanx empowered by the Nova Force would be unstoppable. She tracks down Rider and engages him. With Worldmind giving her tactical information, she was able to avoid the much more powerful Rider, before she incapacitates him. However, she refused to end his life, for her son's sake. However, her moment of hesitation caused her to let her guard down, as Gamora stabbed her in the back. As the life left her, Ko-Rel tried reminding Rider that this is not who is before. He last word was her son's name. Though dead, Ko-Rel proved to a great significance in Rider's freedom from the Phalanx. When she died, the remaining Nova Force that Worldmind imbued in her returned to Rider, giving him the strength to place the virus in remission. A last mental message from her was to ask Rider to save her son. Ko-Rel's personality and image has since been co-opted by the Worldmind as a template to enable it to communicate with the current Corps.

kobak.name: Kobak
kobak.origin: ===Origin=== Kobak Never-Held was one of the mutant inhabitants of Arakko. He was born during the final siege of Arakko, and grew up during the Fallow Years, when Arakko was ruled by Amenth. He and his first lover, Tarlo, resented the demonic occupation. Their dissident thoughts were detected by Vile School omnipaths, and Tarlo shouldered the blame, eventually dying in the Abyssal Prisons, leaving Kobak heartbroken. After Arakko was freed from the grasp of Amenth and relocated to Mars, Kobak challenged Storm to a duel for her place in the Great Ring of Arakko, as he did not accept that a mutant from Krakoa could occupy such an important place reserved for the strongest Arakkii warriors. He was defeated by Storm. He later made a toast to dead lovers with Sunspot, welcoming him to the planet. Kobak also fought against Uranos' forces when he attacked Arakko. ===Great Ring of Arakko=== He ultimately became a member of the Great Ring after having fought Calderak and won against him. He received the seat of Victory, which was once of Genesis. Genesis in fact returned to Arakko and questioned the methods of the Ring after Storm's arrival; Kobak defended her and was, in response, challenged to a fight by Genesis herself. To avoid to make a bloodshed in the Great Ring, Lactuca the Knower teleported Kobak, Storm, Ironfire, Lodus Logos, and Xilo away.

fields.personality: Like all Arakkii mutants, Kobak believes in strength. The trauma of losing his first lover affected him deeply, as he claimed to have wept for a year upon Tarlo's death, and then to never have wept again. While he challenged Storm, believing an outsider such as her had no right to rule the Arakkii, he was quick to accept Krakoan mutant Sunspot after the two shared a toast over their dead lovers.

kobik.name: Kobik
kobik.species: Fragments of different Cosmic Cubes that spontaneously assembled and took human form
kobik.origin: ===Origins and Pleasant Hill=== The being known as Kobik originated from the proposal of the global defence agency known as S.H.I.E.L.D. for a project to use fragments of the ultra-powerful Cosmic Cube objects to reshape reality as the agency would deem necessary. During the course of S.H.I.E.L.D.'s experiments, the fragments unexpectedly and violently merged together, resulting in a new sentient being. That being, Kobik, suffered from a damaged and splintered sense of consciousness, and decided to adopt the form it felt it most resembled in its confusion, a human child. thumb|left|Kobik shortly after her initial "birth" Following the death of the program's leader, Dr. Karen Fowler, another expert in Cosmic Cubes named Erik Selvig was called in to help S.H.I.E.L.D. understand and control Kobik. Motivated by the desire of being truly loved, Kobik decided to go to the one person whom had held dear one of the Cosmic Cubes that now partially composed Kobik, the villain known as Red Skull. The Red Skull took advantage of the child's affinity and naivety and taught her the ways of his evil organization Hydra. Kobik began to lead a double life, using her omnipresence to be in the company of both S.H.I.E.L.D. and the Red Skull at the same time, while keeping this dual-precense a secret from S.H.I.E.L.D. Kobik's innocently deranged set of values caused her to rewrite the past of Selvig's life, inserting a life-long loyalty to Hydra into it, believing that turning a person into a Hydra zealot was something positive. Red Skull's discovery of what Kobik had done to Selvig inspired him to put into motion a plan to have Kobik unknowingly rewrite the history of his greatest enemy, the heroic Steve Rogers. Under the command of the Red Skull, Erik Selvig proposed to S.H.I.E.L.D. the creation of Pleasant Hill, a picture-perfect town inhabited by super-villains whose appearances and memories would be tampered with using Kobik's power to have them forget who they were. The plan was secretly greenlit by S.H.I.E.L.D. Director Maria Hill, hiding it from the rest of the world, and for some amount of time they began shipping super-villains to the town where the villains were transformed into ordinary, harmless citizens without memories of their pasts. Kobik sent two villains, transformed into versions of S.H.I.E.L.D. Director Maria Hill, to prevent the two current superhero Avengers teams (the Avengers and the Avengers Unity Division) from coming to Pleasant Hill. However, both teams discovered that Pleasant Hill existed and arrived anyway, so Kobik captured them upon arriving and turned them into inhabitants of the town. As a part of the Red Skull's plans, one of the incarcerated and transformed villains, the Fixer, subconsciously created a device that returned him to his true self, and he then proceeded to use it on several other inmates, who, being led by the villain Baron Zemo, unleashed a coordinated assault on the town to wreak havoc in revenge for having their lives tampered with. Scared by the sudden destruction being sown by the villains, Kobik ran away and took refuge in her favorite bowling alley. Through the machinations of the Red Skull disguised as one of the town's inhabitants, Kobik was found by Steve Rogers, who at the time had been drained of the Super-Soldier Serum that traditionally gave him powers and made him the hero Captain America. Steve attempted to persuade Kobik to her to use her powers to end the villains' assault but was brutally attacked by a criminal. With Rogers on the brink of death as he fought the criminal, Kobik intervened, and attempted to restore Rogers to his prime condition, before he had been drained of super-soldier serum. However, just as Red Skull had planned, due to Kobik's unwittingly deranged values, she also decided to turn Steve into a Hydra loyalist, creating a new version of history in which that was possible due to Steve undergoing Hydra brainwashing since he was a kid. Kobik subsequently replaced the real Steve with the twisted version of himself she had created. the real one became nothing but a memory inside Kobik's mindscape. thumb|right|Kobik's original human form Nearly directly after this, the two Avengers teams Kobik had trapped in Pleasant Hill began to regain their memories of who they were. Kobik appeared and tried to put the heroes back to "sleep" but they avoided her. As the Avengers were escaping Kobik, however, the newly-awakened villains of Pleasant Hill began mercilessly attacking the de-powered heroes. During the carnage, the hero Deadpool came alongside a distressed Kobik, who was watching with horror as the villains assaulted the super heroes. Deadpool empathized with Kobik over on their shared past of being manipulated by other people outside of their control, and convinced Kobik to do right thing by reviving and healing the heroes, returning them to their full powered selves. After helping the heroes, Kobik disappeared once again, lured to a trap elsewhere i
