kurt wagner moira vii 1.name: Kurt Wagner (Moira-VII.1)
kurt wagner moira vii 1.origin: ===Year 1=== At the start of the Sinister Age, Nightcrawler and Doctor Nemesis were further mutated by Margali Szardos. The two were found by Mother Righteous, who started a quest to free them from the curse, and by Mister Sinister, who locked the two up and created a clone of Nightcrawler to replace him on the Quiet Council. ===Year 5=== During a Council meeting, Storm noticed that Nightcrawler had been replaced by the imposter, making prompting Sinister to emerge, revealing that he was not in the Pit, that all the Council members were under his influence and that Kurt Wagner had been transformed into a monster. thumb|left|200px|Nightcrawler on Year 10. ===Year 10=== Before Year 10, Mother Righteous managed to find Margali Szardos and kill her to break Nightcrawler's curse. From this point, Kurt's DNA became usable for Sinister to create Chimeras. Specifically, Nightcrawler's genes were utilized to create the Legion of the Night, Sinister's squad of assassins. The group turned against Sinister and allied themself with Mother Righteous and started stealing useful objects and weapons; during one of these quests, they met Nightcrawler and collected his memoirs and his writings about the Spark. ===Year 100=== Doctor Nemesis and Nightcrawler were abandoned on Earth, at the Graymalkin Habitat, when it was evacuated. The two were rescued by Wagnerine and the Legion. Once Nightcrawler discovered what Mother Righteous had done with the teaching of the Spark, he became enraged and attacked her. He was promptly killed by Mother Righteous and his body was mummified by his Chimeras, who started questioning Mother Righteous' leadership.

kurt weidner.name: Kurt Weidner
kurt weidner.origin: Kurt Weidner was a Nazi spy that was active in America during World War II. By the fall of 1942, he operated a secret operation in Washington, D.C. that transmitted defense secrets back to Germany. His operation was learned about by the FBI when he was captured. Noticing a resemblance between the spy and FCC agent Jerry Carstairs, the FBI hired Carstairs to pose as Kurt Weidner in order to learn the location of the spies. Despite the fact that Weidner's unnamed boss was ruthless and killed his own agents for even the smallest infraction, he was fooled into thinking that Carstairs was Weidner until the real Weidner broke free and warned him. What the spies were not prepared for was the fact that Carstairs was secretly the costumed hero known as the Black Avenger, who easily rounded up Weidner, his boss and his companions. His fate following the war is unknown.

kuss.name: Kuss
kuss.origin: Kuss was a human gamma mutate that lived on an unnamed world that worshiped the Hulk as a god. He and the Hulk participated in a Godball ritual with Kuss acting as the defender positioned in the rings of rocks that orbited the planet to knock the Godball back to the planet's surface before it could score points. When the banished the Hulk and Pave to a faraway world to punish Hulk for killing some of its members, Monolith was able to prove the Hulk's innocence. However, Kuss was in space and didn't know this, so, he killed the A.U.T.H.O.R.I.T.Y.'s members, forcing Monolith to fight the A.U.T.H.O.R.I.T.Y. until they admitted defeat and return the Hulk and Pave.

kusugutai.name: Kusugutai
kusugutai.origin: Kusugutai was the top underchief of the Skang Kee crime family. When he was first introduced he was being tortured by the Punisher. When other members of his syndicate broke in, he said he would take full responsibility if they killed her. After his men fail to kill her, she hit him before making her escape. As the Punisher made her exit, he ordered his men to stop shooting and informed one to arrange a sit down with the head of the Skang Kee family. Unbeknownst to him, the Punisher had planted a tracking device on him. When he met with his superior, he requested she put the full force of the syndicate behind him, but in response she dismissed him as a joke. It was then that the Punisher made her entrance.

kuthulos.name: Kuthulos
kuthulos.origin: Kuthulos was a scholar-slave of Lady Delcardes, a noblewoman of the he City of Wonders, in Valusia circa 18,500 BC. Wishing to marry Kulra Thorr, a foreigner, Delcardes had her spies gather intel, whom Kuthulos spoke as Saremes, a cat of the Old Race Kull was said he was capable of speech and clairvoyance. Kull offered Saremes a chamber in the Royal Palace, and Kuthulos always remained near her. Thulsa Doom entered Saremes' room through a secret door, bound Kuthulos, hid him behind a drape, and stole his robes. Under Kuthulos' guise, Thulsa Doom, and send Kull to his doom at the Enchanted Domain under a false pretense, while Kuthulos heard, powerless. Escaping doom, Kull returned and was informed that "Kuthulos", rather than Delcardes or Saremes, were to blame for his ordeal. Confronted, Thulsa Doom revealed a captive Kuthulos hidden behind a drape at Delcardes' house, before revealing his true self, before leaving. Kull bore no ill will towards Kuthulos for his forced role in Delcardes' plot, and welcomed him as a a new confidant. After a journey in the mountains, Kull, Brule, Ka-Nu, Kuthulos and the Red Slayers returned to the City of Wonders and stumbled a castle, the Skull of Silence, in the hills of Zalgara. Still many years away from the City of Wonders, Ka-Nu proposed to spent the night. Kutuhulos opposed the notion, recounting the Skull of Silence's story, and the imprisonment there of the Spectre of Silence by Raama. Despite Ka-Nu's and Kuthulos' warnings, Kull broke the chains on the door of the Castle, unleashing the Spectre, which Kull was able to force back before sealing the Skull of Silence once more. Later, Kuthulos was part of the party of the Valusian expedition against the Lemurian pirates. Returning home, the two of five vessels originally gone lost themselves in unmapped waters. Kuthulos notified Kull that they were seemingly on the island where dwelt the Cult of the Leopard. They were welcomed by Dom Vinsala. Due to his methods to quell unrest (which was strengthened by the attacks of Demontur (a man cursed by lycanthropy), Kull, Brule and Kuthulos soon agreed that Vinsala was aggravating the situation. After the isle's people, reinforced by Kull's forces and with the help of Demontur, defeated Vinsala, the Valusians returned home. During the plague, Kuthulos remained within the palace, playing wizard and sorcerer with Brule. When Brule evoked a tale of his home that was reminiscent of his game with Kuthulos, Kull had his circle tell tales to pass time. Kuthulos himself recounted the tale of Yagotha, and how the Old Ones had almost settled in Zalgara more than ten thousands of years ago. Later, Kuthulos discussed of the inexplicable yet real event of the Goblin Moon with Kull. When Kull was missing, Kuthulos agreed with Gonar and Brule to have the time-displaced Conan impersonate the Valusian monarch.

kuu.name: Kuu
kuu.origin: King Kuu ruled over the kingdom of Monoland and it's tribe. When his people brought him the recently captured Tigerman and his allies Professor and Louise Carson he hoped to enslave them to expand his kingdom. They were locked up in a prison, however, they soon escaped thanks to Tigerman's ape companion Rangoo. King Kuu sent his men to recapture them, however, Tigerman and the Carsons escaped. King Kuu's subsequent activities remain unrevealed.

kwabena ware.name: Kwabena Ware
kwabena ware.origin: Kwabena Ware was a Wakanda disillusioned with his king Black Panther following the different tragedies that struck the nation. His village was flooded when the Phoenix-empowered Namor attacked the country, and his brother Kwaku died later on at the hands of the Black Order. Believing that the Black Panther was ignoring the needs of the nation, Kwabena joined the insurgent group known as The People. He was outfitted with repulsor tech and turned into a suicide bomber by the People's ally Zeke Stane. thumb|left The Black Panther abducted Kwabena together with numerous other unconscious suicide bombers when he raided several of the People's bases. When Black Panther was analysing him, Kwabena awoke and berated his king. However, Black Panther refuted Kwabena's claims and even convinced him to abandon the People's cause and their nefarious methods. T'Challa later had Kwabena released and return to one of the People's bases disguised as a soldier so as to look for Ezekiel Stane, while using his soul-searching powers to find them as soon as they came in contact. Once this happened, Black Panther attacked the People alone and appeared to be captured, but in reality, used the opportunity to record Stane confessing that the People's leader Tetu promised him a part of Wakanda for his help. kwai chang.name: Kwai Chang
kwai chang.origin: Kwai Chang was a member of the Golden Tigers, a Chinatown-based gang operating under the command of Chaka Khan. Chang joined Teng, Chen-Wu, and other top enforcers in a coordinated assault on the Meachum Building. Acting under Chaka’s direct leadership, the Golden Tigers sought to overwhelm the premises and assert dominance in their ongoing conflict. Their offensive was swiftly countered by Iron Fist. Despite their numbers and preparation, Chang and his fellow Tigers were decisively outmatched. Iron Fist dismantled the attack with minimal difficulty, leading to the eventual apprehension of the gang members involved.

kwai far.name: Kwai Far
kwai far.origin: Kwai Far is the daughter of Fu Manchu, now going by the name Han, and an unknown woman. She was raised with the intent to act as a bridge between the nations of China and Wakanda. Black Panther and Luke Cage came to negotiate when Han unveiled Kwai Far to the former as a bride for him. Black Panther admitted that she was beautiful, no doubt, but was already in love with someone else. This angered Han who slapped his daughter for failing to seduce the King of Wakanda. As Han sent his man after the two, they were aided by the unexpected arrival of Shang-Chi who had come to rescue his sister. Afterwards, Kwai Far admitted that she was, in fact, in love with Black Panther and did not mind simply going on a date with him. Both Shang-Chi and Luke Cage even managed to get Black Panther to consider it. However, Kwai Far was turned down and has not been seen since.

kwaku anansi.name: Kwaku Anansi
kwaku anansi.origin: ===Early Life=== Kwaku Anansi was the son of the Vodū Sky Father Nyame and the primordial Earth Mother Gaea. According to Ezekiel Sims and the Ashanti tribe in Ghana, Anansi was the first Spider-Man, using his spider-powers to traverse Africa and see all there was to see. Desiring further enlightenment, Anansi struck a bargain with the sky god Nyame, offering his eternal service in return for enlightenment and vanished from the mortal world, his power and knowledge transmitted into spiders everywhere across a Great Web. |thumb|right|Anansi's temple, situated in Wakanda ===War with the Olympians=== In antiquity, Anansi became fascinated with the famous weaver from Athens, Arachne, and secretly made her his first ever herald. However, one day Anansi witnessed the Olympian goddess Athena abducting Arachne due to being led to believe the weaver thought herself as better than her and wanting punish her for this affront. Anansi held out hope Arachne would be returned but as he waited, he eventually ran out of patience and decided to start a war to get his herald back. He led the African gods, both Vodū and Ennead, into attacking the Olympians which were led by the god of war Ares, who was the one who fabricated the rumor about Arachne. The war went on for a while until it was settled by the two pantheons' respective skyfathers, Buluku and Zeus. The two skyfathers admonished their sons for starting a war between their pantheons, but Anansi was at last allowed to get back the body of Arachne. Feeling guilt for her part in the conflict, Athena resurrected Arachne into the form of a creature with a spider body instead of legs in honor of Anansi. Despite this, Anansi still held grudge against the Olympians, specifically Ares, for not receiving any form of punishment. ===Modern Age=== He continued his service to his father in to the modern era, Anansi stood alongside Nyambe, both bearing witness to the primal scream of the Enchantress mourning the death of Heimdall. Anansi's temple in Ghana was used by Spider-Man to defeat the totemic wasp entity Shathra, and was later the site of a duel between Ezekiel Sims and Peter Parker in order to appease the totemic spider deity called the Gatekeeper. ===Council of Godheads=== Anansi attended the Council of Godheads gathered by Athena to prepare a team of godly champions to confront the Skrull Gods. However, he did not provide any champions from amongst his own ranks and openly doubted Athena's intentions, suggesting that the homeless Olympian gods might have designs upon their realms while left unprotected. Anansi participated in a Council of Godheads meeting to talk about Athena's mortal champion Amadeus Cho. He was with the Council when Vali Halfling threatened them to rule over reality as soon as he had reached omniscience. Anansi asked Balder who this Asgardian upstart was and learned that Vali was one of Loki's children. ===Spider-Island=== One day Anansi, disguised as pest specialist A. Nancy, visited the bar & grill that Hercules worked at. They talked for awhile -- about Nancy's blind dog Coltrane and his job. Without revealing his true name Nancy even told Herc about how Anansi once tricked Nyambe into telling Anansi all his stories. Hercules later helped Nancy to sneak into Arachne's apartment so he could steal Arachne's Tapestry. Once outside Nancy was attacked by Elektra, who immediately stole the tapestry, but spared Nancy's life even though Baba Yaga told her to kill him. ===Legion of X=== Later, Anansi (or a fragment thereof) was among several gods across many pantheons used by the Arakkii Mutant Ora Serrata to fabricate Tumult, the Trickster Chimaera. ===Webs of Wakanda=== After Miles Morales was unwittingly turned into a Vampire during the events of Blood Hunt, Black Panther smuggled the young Spider-Man into Wakanda to seek an audience with the Goddess Bast in the hope that she could cure the wallcrawler like she did for him. Unfortunately for the two heroes, Bast was incensed by Miles' presence within her domain as he was already claimed as the herald and champion of her "most loathsome" sibling. Anansi would then suddenly emerge behind Miles to confirm his sister's statement and express an earnest desire to cure the Spider-Man of Varnae's growing corruption. But in order to do so, he must subject Miles to a trial: to provide him with a "good story" in return for purging his vampiric affliction. Believing that all good tales are best started with conflict, Anansi teleported Miles and T'Challa to an arena to face one another as their respective patron Gods spectated. In this spiritual realm, Varnae's spirit took possession of Black Panther and attacked Miles in hopes of taking him as his new vessel. Miles found it difficult to fight him, not only because he didn't want to hurt T'Challa, but also because his attacks had no effect on him. Anansi explained that this ordeal was a trial for him to be deemed worthy as his herald, and soon had Miles fight illusions o

fields.notes: Anansi is also the name of the arachnoid race that was part of the Originators, group of species that inhabited Wakanda before humans and was expelled by humans and Gods of Wakanda. Apparently there is no relationship between Kwaku Anansi and that race, though he was revered in Wakanda. In , Anansi and Bast refer to each other as siblings. It was unclear whether this statement was real, as Bast was described as the granddaughter of Gaea (given the name Neith) and Anansi as the son of Gaea (given the name Asase Ya). Anansi would clarify that he sees every fellow god as a sibling.
fields.trivia: Anansi is named after and partially based on the trickster character from West African Akan mythology , who is often depicted as a spider. The Uzuri Tribe appeared to adhere Anansi as the Shadow King used his likeness to infiltrate the tribe.

kwang che yu.origin: Kwang-Che Yu was a Korean warrior in the 16th century, opposed to the invasion of his country by Japan. Kwang-Che joined a team organized by Japan-born admiral Seagull of the Korean Imperial Navy, also including Cho Yun Chinsong and Portuguese Miguel Mondego Tomar, to protect the inventor of the Korean armored warship Kobukson and his plans against Japanese warlord Raven. The mission was a success, and although Raven managed to kill Seagull, Kwang-Che then killed Raven.

Kwang-Che joined a team organized by Japan-born admiral Seagull of the Korean Imperial Navy, also including Cho Yun Chinsong and Portuguese Miguel Mondego Tomar, to protect the inventor of the Korean armored warship Kobukson and his plans against Japanese warlord Raven. The mission was a success, and although Raven managed to kill Seagull, Kwang-Che then killed Raven.

kwannon.name: Kwannon
kwannon.origin: ===No Mercy=== thumb|right|250px|Being trained by the Hand Molded into an assassin ninja since tender age by a traditional clan of the criminal organization known as the Hand, Kwannon was ironically baptized as such to be “the enemy of peace.” Her training was regarded as a metamorphosis, akin to an insignificant caterpillar transforming into a magnificent butterfly. As a child, she was trafficked to operate as an assassin alongside a fellow orphan, Mitsuki, both under the tutelage of the cruel Master Hayashi who deployed torture to hone his pupils. At the remote mountains of Kyoto, Master Hayashi was responsible for mentoring agents with the potential of developing special powers, justifying his choice for Kwannon, who was a mutant. Usually consumed by violence, during missions, the young Kwannon displayed no mercy at all, slaying targets and enemies swiftly and efficiently with no second thought. Despite having a torturous life, in Mitsuki, Kwannon found a dear friend to whom she could relate. Mitsuki had the ability to commune with Yokai spirits, that proved essential in an assignment aimed at collecting the soul-eating Equinox Blade for Hayashi. The wielder of the sword had been transformed into a devilish Oni. While engaging in battle against him, Kwannon's mutant powers activated and she executed the creature using telepathy to deactivate his mind. Due to her inferior performance, Mitsuki was executed by Master Hayashi, which represented a traumatic event for Kwannon. Endowed with mutant telepathic abilities, Kwannon cultivated a notorious reputation in Japan as an efficient killer who could delve into others' thoughts, operating as a loyal and merciless member of her clan. However, as a Hand operative, Kwannon's path took a turn when she fell in love with a young man and bore a daughter, which displeased her masters. Her beloved was slain, and her newborn child was separated from her. In a twisted display of so-called mercy, the baby was marked with a butterfly-shaped tattoo behind her neck in order to make her recognizable if fate ever brought mother and daughter together again. However, Kwannon never again encountered her lost daughter, baptized Himeko. thumb|left|325px|Breaking free from her masters A crucial moment in Kwannon's career unfolded after she was assigned the task of eliminating a traitor within her clan. As she carried out the execution, empathy overwhelmed her due to a psychic glimpse of the love her target harbored for his wife and unborn child. Touched by compassion, Kwannon rebelliously aided the family go underground rather than murdering them, defying the explicit orders she had received. Another clandestine act of mercy occurred during a mission in which Kwannon chose not to destroy a menacing artificial intelligence named Apoth. This decision led Apoth to develop an obsessive connection with Kwannon, perceiving its savior as its true creator. These manifestations of Kwannon's resilience against the psychological torment imposed upon her culminated in her turning against her masters and assassinating them. Her liberation paralleled the emergence of a butterfly from its chrysalis, but simultaneously transformed Kwannon into the weapon of destruction her dark overseers had always intended her to become. thumb|right|300px|Operating as Lord Nyoirin's prime assassin Knowing nothing else but violence, Kwannon worked as an assassin by trade, rising to prominence as the main operative serving Japanese crime lord Nyoirin. Concurrently, she engaged in a romantic relationship with Matsu'o Tsurayaba, a high-ranking figure within the Hand. As the interests of Nyoirin and the Hand came into conflict, Kwannon found herself honor-bound to face her lover in a lethal duel. The fight ensued against the backdrop of an ocean cliff and resulted in Kwannon's precipitous fall. She sustained injuries that left her with debilitating brain damage. The prognosis for the comatose Kwannon offered no glimmer of hope for recovering, which weighed heavily on Tsurayaba. ===Revanche=== thumb|left|275px|Trapped in a coma Conveniently, the telepathic member of the X-Men Betsy Braddock, a.k.a. Psylocke, was found washed up on the shore of the Hand's island base in the South China Sea. Her arrival, a consequence of passing through the Siege Perilous, posited a solution to Kwannon's predicament. Determined to restore Kwannon, Tsurayaba sought the assistance of the sorceress Spiral, a begrudging servant of Mojo, who had previously shown interest in Psylocke. Tsurayaba believed that Kwannon's limited psychic powers would allow her mind to withstand contact with a high-level telepath like Psylocke, recovering her from her coma. Spiral's penchant for trickery and deception led her to transpose the minds of the two women into each other's bodies. Kwannon's perfected body became inhabited by Braddock's telepathic mind, while her fractured psyche lived on Braddock's moribund body. Tsurayaba transformed Psylocke into a loyal

fields.trivia: The name "Kwannon" (観音, in Kanji character) is an archaic transliteration of her namesake, the bodhisattva of mercy, which would be rendered as "Kan'non" in current Japanese, pronounced as [kanːoɴ]. The name "Revanche" ([ɹəˈvɑ̃ʃ]) is not simply an alternate derivative of the word "revenge", but rather means a "policy designed to recover lost territory or status." From French origin, it is pronounced as [ʁəˈvɑ̃ʃ] in French. The name "Psylocke" ([ˈsaɪ.lɑːk] SEYE-lok) is assumed by some fans to be a wordplay with the words "psyche", "key" and "lock". As "psyche" is pronounced as "psy-key", "Psylocke" would be pronounced as "psy-lock".

kyi.name: Kyi
kyi.origin: Kyi was a young gymnast who wanted to join Taskmaster's Academy to train and become a mercenary. He infiltrated the Academy by tagging after Diamondback and Siren. Taskmaster at first refused to accept young kid, but Kyi managed to convince him by demonstrating his teleporting powers. Kyi soon discovered that the Academy was full of explosives, installed by Diamondback. Taskmaster found where she was and Kyi tried to open portal to teleport himself, Taskmaster and Siren there and the Academy exploded in the last moment. Either due to the explosion or for another reason, but the portal was affected and malfunctioned; Siren was teleported back to her own reality, and where Kyi and Taskmaster ended up is unknown.

kyklops.name: Kyklops
kyklops.origin: The Kyklops was a massive robot super weapon that was designed by the Enclave and unleashed on New York as the Enclave was taking external damage. The war machine's reign of terror was stopped when the Incredible Hulk appeared and assaulted the robot, throwing vehicles at its massive optic, and throwing its foot when it attempted to stomp on him. Eventually Hulk managed to tear the robot apart, destroying it. The Enclave would send an army of other weaker Kyklops to attack high priority targets and guard major locations, though they too were destroyed by either the Hulk or the U.S. Army.

kyknos.name: Kyknos
kyknos.species: Half-human demigod son of the Greek God Ares and a mortal woman
kyknos.origin: Kyknos was the son of the mortal Mycenaean princess Pelopia and of Ares, the Greek God of war. He decided to build a temple to his father, but during this effort he was killed by Hercules, thus sparking Ares' long-standing rivalry with the Prince of Power. Kyknos went to Hades when he died, and remained there for thousands of years. When Hercules journeyed to the underworld to recover Zeus, Kyknos was part of the jury that Hercules had to beat to free him. During Norman Osborn's period in power, Hera came to Hades and recruited Kyknos to be her new god of war. In exchange, all he had to do was kill his father. Kyknos agreed, but was killed by his father.

kyle brock.origin: Kyle Brock was an NYPD officer on duty when he was shot by criminals and left to die. He was brought to a New York hospital where he was taken by the Egyptian god of death, Seth, and given a second chance. Seth needed his Asgardian enemy, Hogun the Grim, to join him permanently in the realm of death, so he tried to trick Brock and his companions into ending his life. Kyle Brock would be rewarded by being made whole once more able to live out his life with his wife and family. Seth knew that a mortal could never accomplish this task so he gave Brock the incredible powers of Earth Lord. The punishment for failing his mission would return Brock to the death god's realm forever. As Earth Lord and his teammates fought the Thunder god, Thor, who was protecting Hogun, he had doubts about what he was doing and decided to rethink his position. He and the other members of Earth Force left the scene only to return with the hope that they may join Thor in his fight against Seth. Together with some of the most powerful beings in the universe, Earth Lord turned on his former master. Seth believed that with enough time Earth Lord may have been able to defeat him, but Seth wasn't about to give him that luxury. Earth Force was no match for their former master and was left to die. Seth was eventually defeated and Earth Lord along with the members of Earth Force was healed by the other Heliopolitan gods and was returned to Earth. Sometime after Brock was released from the hospital, he and his partner trailed a gang known as the Bloody Claws to an apartment building. In a hail of gunfire Brock's partner was shot and believed he would die. This made Brock think of his near-death experience which endowed him with the power of Earth Lord. As his partner fell unconscious, Brock grabbed the sign of Aton that was tattooed in his palm and made the stunning transformation into Earth Lord. The Bloody Claws were no match for Earth Lord's power and were quickly subdued. Now that the gang was finished and Brock's partner was safe, he shouted over the rooftops that Earth Lord was here to stay. Brock was eventually called to a location, along with other police units, when Bloodaxe seemed to be running amok and endangering an innocent woman's life. The special task force Code: Blue was called in to deal with this super powered menace, but Brock knew they wouldn't be able to stop Bloodaxe alone. When no one was looking, Brock transformed himself into the giant Earth Lord and sent a signal to the other members of Earth Force, Skyhawk and Wind Warrior. Earth Lord engaged Bloodaxe on his own, which enabled police to rescue the woman, Susan Austin, but his teammates soon showed up to assist. Together Earth Force, Code: Blue and a little help from the astral form of Doctor Strange were able to stop the menace of Bloodaxe. The current whereabouts of Earth Lord are unknown.

kyle dansig.name: Kyle Dansig
kyle dansig.origin: Kyle Dansig was an FBI agent working as part of the Project Chimera, a organization made to capture and brainwash mutants into government agents, run by Virus. When a team of mutants led by Logan started raiding Project Chimera bases and freeing mutant prisoners, including Dansig's own sons Shadowshift and Scout, Virus sent Bolivar Trask's Sentinels against the team. When the Sentinels attacked Logan's team's stronghold, Dansig had a change of heart, running into the flames to save his sons. Charles Xavier covered their escape, making all the surrounding government agents think the three of them perished in the fire.

kyle gibney.name: Kyle Gibney
kyle gibney.species: Mutant; later genetically enhanced with Wyre's DNA. Category:Genetically Engineered
kyle gibney.origin: ===Early Life=== When Kyle Gibney's mutant powers began to emerge at an early age, he was left with a freakish appearance. Horrified, his parents kicked him out of his home, and he was left wandering the streets. Eventually found by the subversive organization, the Secret Empire, Gibney was experimented upon in their attempts to create a perfect killing machine. As a part of the experiment, Gibney was injected with DNA from the assassin Wyre, which left Gibney near-mindless, animalistic, and uncontrollable. Wyre later rebelled and destroyed the Secret Empire's headquarters. ===Gamma Flight Trainee=== Gibney was found by agents of the Canadian government and given over to Department H, then headed by James Hudson as a sanctioned program for developing Canada's superhero teams. Hudson placed Gibney in the entry-level Gamma Flight with the code-name Wild Child. (Like all recruits, those who developed their powers sufficiently would be placed in the premiere team, Alpha Flight.) During his training, Wild Child was mentored by Wolverine until he left to join the X-Men. During one of their training sessions Kyle lost control and almost ripped Stich's face off, Wolverine wanted to kill him him but Hudson stopped him. Department H provided Kyle with special pills to suppress his animalistic tendencies, which were a side-effect of his mutation. ===Omega Flight=== Unfortunately, the government disbanded the Department H program and, by extension, its hero teams. Gibney's subsequent activities remain unrevealed until Delphine Courtney and Jerry Jaxon recruited him for Omega Flight. Jaxon hoped to destroy Hudson and his Alpha Flight, which had reassembled as a private team, but Omega Flight was captured by Alpha Flight and its members imprisoned. Gibney managed to break out only once, and in his rampage, began killing indiscriminately. Nearly killing Heather Hudson, it took Wolverine to hunt him down and capture him again. ===Gamma Flight=== During a period of time in which Alpha Flight was believed dead, the Canadian government decided to reinstate a fully-sanctioned hero team under the name Gamma Flight. Gibney was recruited for the team and pardoned for his previous activities. When Alpha Flight reappeared, the two teams clashed, and Alpha Flight was forced to go on trial. Ultimately, Alpha Flight rejected the government's support and decided to operate independently once more. Gamma Flight continued as the government-sponsored team, and the two teams eventually met again to fight the evil Llan the Sorcerer. Gamma Flight was nearly destroyed in the final battle, but Llan was defeated. Afterward, the two teams combined into one, with Alpha Flight again reinstated as Canada's official superhero group. ===Becoming Weapon Omega=== Kyle soon found himself slipping into his bestial nature more and more often. One time in particular, he savagely went on another rampage, in the process attacking his teammate Pathway. Gamma Flight's former leader, Nemesis, teleported Kyle away to an unknown location, professing to have a solution. He reappeared months later as Weapon Omega, mysteriously cured of his animalistic rages and possessing a handsome appearance. He helped Alpha Flight on numerous occasions, soon joining their team once more. ===Aurora=== To further disassociate from his past, Kyle took a new code-name, Wildheart. During this time, Gibney and his teammate Aurora fell in love and began a relationship. However, Kyle eventually began to mutate back to his ugly appearance. Since he could not stand to be seen that way by his lover, he left, unaware that his sudden departure would cause Aurora's fragile psyche to deteriorate even further. ===X-Factor=== Kyle Gibney, now calling himself Wild Child once more, accepted an offer to join the United States' sanctioned mutant team, X-Factor. This caused a bit of friction between Gibney and X-Factor's associate, Sabretooth, who was impressed into service. Eventually, however, Gibney's body began mutating even further, and he quit the team to explore his new mutations and to find his true self. ===Weapon X=== left|200px|thumb|Aurora & Wildchild Somehow, Kyle ended up in custody of the new Weapon X program, under the auspices of the mysterious Director, who hoped to use the program's mutants for the benefit of humankind, even if that meant performing deadly missions and interning mutant captives. The program's scientist experimented on Kyle, who became more intelligent but more feral-looking, and was once again dubbed Wild Child. The Director found that Gibney had been twisted so many times that he no longer held an identity of his own, needing only minimal suggestions via conventional methods to follow orders like a machine or an animal. One of Gibney's initial assignments was to recruit mutants for the Weapon X program. kyle grobe.name: Kyle Grobe
kyle grobe.origin: In the year 2092 of Earth-9485 (a divergent Earth-928), Kyle Grobe and his son Darrion were working on a project for the technology company Alchemax involving time travel by creating a protective armor called a "time shell." The two discovered a dimension comprised of kinetic energy (the same dimension from which the hero Speedball drew his powers), and Darrion suggested this would be an alternative to the time shell, as time had no meaning within the dimension. However, his father refused, and, in the process of rushing the project to completion, Kyle Grobe was swept into the time stream and merged with the time shell, dying himself and creating the techno-organic being called Advent. As Advent, Kyle Grobe manipulated the past to change his future. His son, Darrion, protected from the alteration by having creating a pocket reality during the experiment, was determined to fix the mess his father created. He found Speedball in the kinetic dimension and created a duplicate body of the hero, transferred his own consciousness into it, and replaced Speedball with the duplicate. For some time, Darrion lived as Speedball and with Speedball's teammates, the New Warriors. However, Darrion's presence created chaos with time itself, and the villainous Sphinx confronted the New Warriors, ultimately drawing Advent to the scene. The Sphinx killed the Speedball duplicate and he and Advent escaped. The Warrior Timeslip was with the duplicate as it died, and she received Darrion's memories. Timeslip used her knowledge and powers to transport the New Warriors to the future. There, a holographic persona of Darrion further helped the Warriors to undo all of Advent's manipulations. Ultimately, the team had to enter the kinetic dimension and join the true Speedball in defeating Advent before returning home.

kyle lacon.name: Kyle Lacon
kyle lacon.origin: Kyle Lacon was the member of a biker gang in New York City. He hired Deadpool to kill one of his fellow gang members, Rocko. Klye and Deadpool staged an encounter with the gang at a local cinema, and Deadpool confronted Rocko. After killing Rocko, Deadpool had Kyle fill out the necessary paperwork, and tried to charge him a penalty fee for not having disclosed in advance that Rocko was a superhuman. When Kyle refused, Deadpool stole his motorbike. Kyle was left with the rest of the gang, who beat him up for having put a hit out on Rocko.

Klye and Deadpool staged an encounter with the gang at a local cinema, and Deadpool confronted Rocko. After killing Rocko, Deadpool had Kyle fill out the necessary paperwork, and tried to charge him a penalty fee for not having disclosed in advance that Rocko was a superhuman. When Kyle refused, Deadpool stole his motorbike. Kyle was left with the rest of the gang, who beat him up for having put a hit out on Rocko.
